title: "Beating cuBLAS on an H100"

# Beating cuBLAS on an H100
NVIDIA's Hopper H100 microarchitecture introduced two revolutionary hardware subsystems:

### 1. Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA)

In pre-Hopper architectures, threads in a warp explicitly load data from global memory into registers, then write from registers into shared memory. 
TMA executes multidimensional tensor transfers (e.g. 2D/3D tiles) directly between global HBM and shared memory **asynchronously in hardware**, completely bypassing the register file and consuming zero SM ALU cycles.

### 2. Warp Specialization

Instead of every thread in a block performing both memory loading and arithmetic:
- **Producer Warps (1-2 warps):** Issue asynchronous TMA copy instructions to fetch upcoming tiles into double-buffered shared memory.
- **Consumer Warps (Warp Groups):** Execute continuous WGMMA matrix multiply instructions without ever pausing for memory latency.
- Hardware barrier arrive/wait primitives (`cuda::barrier`) synchronize producers and consumers with cycle-level precision.
